name: The Zoram Strand
summary: Naga now threaten Ashenvale from the Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar sends Alliance champions to scour the northwestern coast, where an ancient ruined city lies. Stopping the naga protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves’ distant past.

sections.title: Shadows on the Shore
sections.body: At Ashenvale’s northwestern edge, the Zoram Strand meets the Veiled Sea. Its shore lies northwest of Astranaar, where the forest canopy gives way to the coast. The beach was quiet for ages, its stones left from a civilization shattered ten millennia ago. Now Wrathtail naga have come out of the dark tides in force. They have made a hostile beachhead on the borders of night elven territory, and threaten to press inland.

sections.title: The Drowned City of Zoram
sections.body: The city of Zoram lies shattered beneath the surf, submerged during the Great Sundering. For ages, it remained abandoned and nearly forgotten by the kaldorei. The naga’s sudden arrival among its ruins stirs bitter memories among Astranaar’s defenders. Sentinels such as Shindrell Swiftfire know the invaders as twisted cousins, born of their own ancient catastrophe. They will not let the depths claim the shore again.

faq.answer: The Zoram Strand runs along Ashenvale’s rugged northwestern shore, facing the Veiled Sea. Ancient Zoram, a kaldorei city swallowed by the ocean during the Sundering ten thousand years ago, lies there.

faq.q: Why are the naga attacking Ashenvale's coast?
faq.answer: The Sentinels in Astranaar do not know exactly why the naga are attacking Ashenvale’s coast. Their military camps and aggression threaten the forests, so the night elves strike before the naga can advance.
Shindrell Swiftfire is a night elf sentinel stationed in Astranaar. She watches for threats to Ashenvale and organizes strikes against hostile incursions, including the naga on the coast.

faq.q: What history do the night elves share with the naga?
faq.answer: The naga were once Highborne night elves who served Queen Azshara. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Sundering, they were dragged into the abyssal depths and transformed into serpentine creatures. Their kinship makes every encounter bitter for the modern kaldorei.

faq.q: What happens after clearing the Zoram Strand?
faq.answer: After the naga are thinned along the strand, Shindrell Swiftfire sends Alliance defenders to face other aerial threats along the border. She directs scouts south toward Stonetalon to deal with vicious pridewings.

faq.q: Is the Horde also present at the Zoram Strand?
faq.answer: Yes. Alliance champions from Astranaar hunt the shoreline’s naga, while the Horde holds Zoram’gar Outpost, a fortified seaside outpost on the strand. The Horde contests the region and battles both the naga and the Alliance.

angles.text: For a night elf, every naga slain on the strand recalls Azshara’s arrogance and the Sundering that broke the ancient world. Sentinels will not let these twisted kin regain ground in Kalimdor.
For the Alliance, securing Ashenvale’s western flank keeps Astranaar from being caught between coastal invaders and Horde lumber operations.
As a hunter, you can use the wind-battered coast and broken ruins as vantage points to track amphibious raiders emerging from the breakers.
